transcript_turns.text: People’s rights have been abused.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I met a man who spent eight months in prison, wasn’t even allowed to call his lawyer, wasn’t allowed to get — finally, Senator Dick Durbin of Illinois intervened and was able to get him out.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This is in our country, folks, the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve got sneak-and-peek searches that are allowed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve got people allowed to go into churches now and political meetings without any showing of potential criminal activity or otherwise.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, I voted for the Patriot Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Ninety-nine United States senators voted for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the president’s been very busy running around the country using what I just described to you as a reason to say I’m wishy-washy, that I’m a flip-flopper.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now that’s not a flip-flop.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe in the Patriot Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We need the things in it that coordinate the FBI and the CIA.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We need to be stronger on terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But you know what we also need to do as Americans is never let the terrorists change the Constitution of the United States in a way that disadvantages our rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You know, Elizabeth, I really respect your — the feeling that’s in your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I understand it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I know the morality that’s prompting that question, and I respect it enormously.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But like Nancy Reagan, and so many other people — you know, I was at a forum with Michael J.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Fox the other day in New Hampshire, who’s suffering from Parkinson’s, and he wants us to do stem cell, embryonic stem cell.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And this fellow stood up, and he was quivering.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: His whole body was shaking from the nerve disease, the muscular disease that he had.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And he said to me and to the whole hall, he said, “You know, don’t take away my hope, because my hope is what keeps me going.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” Chris Reeve is a friend of mine.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Chris Reeve exercises every single day to keep those muscles alive for the day when he believes he can walk again, and I want him to walk again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think we can save lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think we can do ethically guided embryonic stem-cell research.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We have 100,000 to 200,000 embryos that are frozen in nitrogen today from fertility clinics.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: These weren’t taken from abortion or something like that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’re from a fertility clinic.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And they’re either going to be destroyed or left frozen.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I believe if we have the option, which scientists tell us we do, of curing Parkinson’s, curing diabetes, curing, you know, some kind of a, you know, paraplegic or quadriplegic or, you know, a spinal cord injury, anything, that’s the nature of the human spirit.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think it is respecting life to reach for that cure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think it is respecting life to do it in an ethical way.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the president has chosen a policy that makes it impossible for our scientists to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I want the future, and I think we have to grab it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Embryonic stem-cell research requires the destruction of life to create a stem cell.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m the first president ever to allow funding — federal funding — for embryonic stem-cell research.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I did to because I too hope that we’ll discover cures from the stem cells and from the research derived.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I think we’ve got to be very careful in balancing the ethics and the science.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I made the decision we wouldn’t spend any more money beyond the 70 lines, 22 of which are now in action, because science is important, but so is ethics, so is balancing life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To destroy life to save life is — it’s one of the real ethical dilemmas that we face.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is going to be hundreds of experiments off the 22 lines that now exist that are active, and hopefully we find a cure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But as well, we need to continue to pursue adult stem-cell research.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I helped double the NIH budget to $28 billion a year to find cures.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the approach I took is one that I think is a balanced and necessary approach, to balance science and the concerns for life.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, you talk about walking a waffle line — he says he’s allowed it, which means he’s going to allow the destruction of life up to a certain amount and then he isn’t going to allow it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know how you draw that line.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But let me tell you, point blank, the lines of stem cells that he’s made available, every scientist in the country will tell you, “Not adequate,” because they’re contaminated by mouse cells, and because there aren’t 60 or 70 — they’re are only about 11 to 20 now — and there aren’t enough to be able to do the research because they’re contaminated.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to open up the possibilities of this research.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And when I am president, I’m going to do it because we have to.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me make sure you understand my decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Those stem- cells lines already existed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The embryo had already been destroyed prior to my decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I had to make the decision to destroy more life, so do we continue to destroy life — I made the decision to balance science and ethics.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not telling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I really don’t have — haven’t picked anybody yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Plus, I want them all voting for me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would pick somebody who would not allow their personal opinion to get in the way of the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would pick somebody who would strictly interpret the Constitution of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you a couple of examples, I guess, of the kind of person I wouldn’t pick.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wouldn’t pick a judge who said that the Pledge of Allegiance couldn’t be said in a school because it had the words “under God” in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s an example of a judge allowing personal opinion to enter into the decision-making process as opposed to a strict interpretation of the Constitution.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Another example would be the Dred Scott case, which is where judges, years ago, said that the Constitution allowed slavery because of personal property rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s a personal opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what the Constitution says.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Constitution of the United States says we’re all — you know, it doesn’t say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t speak to the equality of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so, I would pick people that would be strict constructionists.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got plenty of lawmakers in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Legislators make law; judges interpret the Constitution.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I suspect one of us will have a pick at the end of next year — the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the kind of judge I’m going to put on there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No litmus test except for how they interpret the Constitution.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Charlie.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: A few years ago when he came to office, the president said — these are his words — “What we need are some good conservative judges on the courts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” And he said also that his two favorite justices are Justice Scalia and Justice Thomas.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: So you get a pretty good sense of where he’s heading if he were to appoint somebody.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, here’s what I believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe we need a good conservative judge, and I don’t believe we need a good liberal judge.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe we need a good judge of that kind of definition on either side.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I subscribe to the Justice Potter Stewart standard.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He was a justice on the Supreme Court of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And he said the mark of a good judge, good justice, is that when you’re reading their decision, their opinion, you can’t tell if it’s written by a man or woman, a liberal or a conservative, a Muslim, a Jew or a Christian.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You just know you’re reading a good judicial decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: What I want to find, if I am privileged to have the opportunity to do it — and the Supreme Court of the United States is at stake in this race, ladies and gentlemen.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The future of things that matter to you — in terms of civil rights, what kind of Justice Department you’ll have, whether we’ll enforce the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Will we have equal opportunity?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Will women’s rights be protected?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Will we have equal pay for women, which is going backwards?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Will a woman’s right to choose be protected?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: These are constitutional rights, and I want to make sure we have judges who interpret the Constitution of the United States according to the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I would say to that person exactly what I will say to you right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I cannot tell you how deeply I respect the belief about life and when it begins.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m a Catholic, raised a Catholic.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I was an altar boy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Religion has been a huge part of my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It helped lead me through a war, leads me today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I can’t take what is an article of faith for me and legislate it for someone who doesn’t share that article of faith, whether they be agnostic, atheist, Jew, Protestant, whatever.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I can’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I can counsel people.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I can talk reasonably about life and about responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I can talk to people, as my wife Teresa does, about making other choices, and about abstinence, and about all these other things that we ought to do as a responsible society.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But as a president, I have to represent all the people in the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I have to make that judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, I believe that you can take that position and not be pro- abortion, but you have to afford people their constitutional rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And that means being smart about allowing people to be fully educated, to know what their options are in life, and making certain that you don’t deny a poor person the right to be able to have whatever the constitution affords them if they can’t afford it otherwise.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I think it’s important.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I think it’s important for the United States, for instance, not to have this rigid ideological restriction on helping families around the world to be able to make a smart decision about family planning.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You’ll help prevent AIDS.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You’ll help prevent unwanted children, unwanted pregnancies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You’ll actually do a better job, I think, of passing on the moral responsibility that is expressed in your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I truly respect it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m trying to decipher that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My answer is, we’re not going to spend taxpayers’ money on abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is an issue that divides America, but certainly reasonable people can agree on how to reduce abortions in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I signed the partial-birth — the ban on partial-birth abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a brutal practice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s one way to help reduce abortions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent voted against the ban.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think there ought to be parental notification laws.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s against them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I signed a bill called the Unborn Victims of Violence Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In other words, if you’re a mom and you’re pregnant and you get killed, the murderer gets tried for two cases, not just one.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent was against that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: These are reasonable ways to help promote a culture of life in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it is a worthy goal in America to have every child protected by law and welcomed in life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I also think we ought to continue to have good adoption law as an alternative to abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we need to promote maternity group homes, which my administration has done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Culture of life is really important for a country to have if it’s going to be a hospitable society.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, again, the president just said, categorically, my opponent is against this, my opponent is against that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You know, it’s just not that simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: No, I’m not.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m against the partial-birth abortion, but you’ve got to have an exception for the life of the mother and the health of the mother under the strictest test of bodily injury to the mother.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, with respect to parental notification, I’m not going to require a 16-or 17-year-old kid who’s been raped by her father and who’s pregnant to have to notify her father.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: So you got to have a judicial intervention.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And because they didn’t have a judicial intervention where she could go somewhere and get help, I voted against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s never quite as simple as the president wants you to believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s pretty simple when they say: Are you for a ban on partial birth abortion?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes or no?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he was given a chance to vote, and he voted no.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s just the way it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s a vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It came right up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s clear for everybody to see.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And as I said: You can run but you can’t hide the reality.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Put a head fake on us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Hi, Linda.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have made a lot of decisions, and some of them little, like appointments to boards you never heard of, and some of them big.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in a war, there’s a lot of — there’s a lot of tactical decisions that historians will look back and say: He shouldn’t have done that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He shouldn’t have made that decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll take responsibility for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m human.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But on the big questions, about whether or not we should have gone into Afghanistan, the big question about whether we should have removed somebody in Iraq, I’ll stand by those decisions, because I think they’re right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s really what you’re — when they ask about the mistakes, that’s what they’re talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re trying to say, “Did you make a mistake going into Iraq?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” And the answer is, “Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” It was the right decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Duelfer report confirmed that decision today, because what Saddam Hussein was doing was trying to get rid of sanctions so he could reconstitute a weapons program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the biggest threat facing America is terrorists with weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We knew he hated us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We knew he’d been — invaded other countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We knew he tortured his own people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On the tax cut, it’s a big decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I did the right decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our recession was one of the shallowest in modern history.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, you asked what mistakes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I made some mistakes in appointing people, but I’m not going to name them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to hurt their feelings on national TV.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But history will look back, and I’m fully prepared to accept any mistakes that history judges to my administration, because the president makes the decisions, the president has to take the responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe the president made a huge mistake, a catastrophic mistake, not to live up to his own standard, which was: build a true global coalition, give the inspectors time to finish their job and go through the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: process to its end and go to war as a last resort.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I ask each of you just to look into your hearts, look into your guts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Gut-check time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Was this really going to war as a last resort?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president rushed our nation to war without a plan to win the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And simple things weren’t done.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s why Senator Lugar says: incompetent in the delivery of services.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s why Senator Hagel, Republican, says, you know: beyond pitiful, beyond embarrassing, in the zone of dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t guard 850,000 tons of ammo.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That ammo is now being used against our kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Ten thousand out of 12,000 Humvees aren’t armored.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I visited some of those kids with no limbs today, because they didn’t have the armor on those vehicles.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They didn’t have the right body armor.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met parents who’ve on the Internet gotten the armor to send their kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: There is no bigger judgment for a president of the United states than how you take a nation to war.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And you can’t say, because Saddam might have done it 10 years from now, that’s a reason; that’s an excuse.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He complains about the fact our troops don’t have adequate equipment, yet he voted against the $87 billion supplemental I sent to the Congress and then issued one of the most amazing quotes in political history: “I actually did vote for the $87 billion before I voted against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” Saddam Hussein was a risk to our country, ma’am.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he was a risk that — and this is where we just have a difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The truth of that matter is, if you listen carefully, Saddam would still be in power if he were the president of the United States, “And the world would be a lot better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Not necessarily be in power, but here’s what I’ll say about the $87 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I made a mistake in the way I talk about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He made a mistake in invading Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Which is a worse decision?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, I voted the way I voted because I saw that he had the policy wrong and I wanted accountability.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t want to give a slush fund to Halliburton.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I also thought the wealthiest people in America ought to pay for it, ladies and gentlemen.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He wants your kids to pay for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I wanted us to pay for it, since we’re at war.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’s a bad decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Do you want to go first?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Either way.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Charlie, thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And thank you all.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, all of you, for taking part.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thanks for your questions tonight, very, very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Obviously the president and I both have very strong convictions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I respect him for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we have a very different view about how to make America stronger and safer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I will never cede the authority of our country or our security to any other nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ll never give a veto over American security to any other entity — not a nation, not a country, not an institution.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I know, as I think you do, that our country is strongest when we lead the world, when we lead strong alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the way Eisenhower and Reagan and Kennedy and others did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We are not doing that today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We need to.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan that will help us go out and kill and find the terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I will not stop in our efforts to hunt down and kill the terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I’ll also have a better plan of how we’re going to deal with Iraq: training the Iraqi forces more rapidly, getting our allies back to the table with a fresh start, with new credibility, with a president whose judgment the rest of the world trusts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: In addition to that, I believe we have a crisis here at home, a crisis of the middle class that is increasingly squeezed, health-care costs going up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan to provide health care to all Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan to provide for our schools so we keep the standards but we help our teachers teach and elevate our schools by funding No Child Left Behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan to protect the environment so that we leave this place in better shape to our children than we were handed it by our parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s the test.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe America’s best days are ahead of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m an optimist, but we have to make the right choices, to be fiscally responsible and to create the new jobs of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can do this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I ask you for the privilege of leading our nation to be stronger at home and respected again in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Charlie, thanks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you all very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s been enjoyable.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The great contest for the presidency is about the future, who can lead, who can get things done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been through a lot together as a country — been through a recession, corporate scandals, war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And yet think about where we are: Added 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 9 million new jobs over the past 13 months.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The farm income in America is high.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Small businesses are flourishing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Homeownership rate is at an all-time high in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re on the move.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Tonight I had a chance to discuss with you what to do to keep this economy going: keep the taxes low, don’t increase the scope of the federal government, keep regulations down, legal reform, a health- care policy that does not empower the federal government but empowers individuals, and an energy plan that will help us become less dependent on foreign sources of energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And abroad, we’re at war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it requires a president who is steadfast and strong and determined.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I vowed to the American people after that fateful day of September the 11th that we would not rest nor tire until we’re safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The 9/11 Commission put out a report that said America is safer but not yet safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is more work to be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll stay on the hunt on Al Qaida.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll deny sanctuary to these terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll make sure they do not end up with weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the great nexus.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The great threat to our country is that these haters end up with weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But our long-term security depends on our deep faith in liberty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll continue to promote freedom around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Freedom is on the march.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Tomorrow, Afghanistan will be voting for a president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In Iraq, we’ll be having free elections, and a free society will make this world more peaceful.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: God bless.
